summary: Reject octal and hexadecimal escapes whose values exceed one byte.
explanation: `Unescape.BasicFunction` checks each entry in `bad`, including `"\\777"` and `"\\xABCD"`. For those inputs, `CUnescape(e, &out, &error)` returns true and leaves `error.empty()` true, though the test expects false and a nonempty error; the no-error overload also returns true instead of false. Both byte-range checks were incorrectly conditional on `leave_nulls_escaped`, which is false for `CUnescape`. Remove that condition. Since hexadecimal escapes may contain arbitrarily many digits, accumulate only while the value fits in a byte and remember overflow while consuming the rest of the escape; this prevents unsigned wraparound from making an oversized value appear valid.
